method.targets: analytic forward and backward derivatives of the actual min/max/clip renderer; also their average
method.direction_units: each target normalized to length one; coefficients for physical-unit derivatives obtained by multiplying by its stored norm
method.reconstruction: orthogonal projection; coefficients are target dot basis vector; no regularization or physical-knob matching
method.single: best possible scalar multiple of any one of the five leading SVD vectors
method.full: all sampled singular directions above the stated signal cutoff, not a completed ambient basis
method.limit: SVD of exact infinitesimal directional derivatives; known-renderer control, not a data-only estimator
method.oracle: true target vectors supplied to the coefficient solve; this tests representability, not discovery of weights
method.bounds: two-sided root neighborhoods and walk states can extend beyond default ranges; stroke remains positive and unclipped
